text: In a small pond a mother duck waits for her eggs to hatch. One of her eggs is much larger than the others.
The eggs start to hatch, and yellow fluffy ducklings pop out until there is only one left.
The last duckling looks different. He has grey feathers, a long neck, and big feet.
The other ducklings begin to whisper, "He does not look like us. Why is he so weird?"
The grey duckling is upset at the whispering.
scene4.prompt: What should the grey duckling do?

choices.text: Get angry and yell at them for being mean.
Walk away and find a quiet place to calm down.
Run away from the rest of the family forever.

text: Yelling does not help the duckling feel better. When feeling big emotions, it is a good idea to calm down first.

choices.text: Walk away and find a quiet place to calm down.

text: Walking away to calm down gives the duckling time to handle his big emotions safely.

scene7.prompt: Let's have the grey duckling try something else.

choices.text: Get angry and yell at them for being mean.

text: The duckling takes deep breaths. He walks over to a quiet patch. He is still sad, but feels better now that he is calm.

The duckling leaves the pond and goes on a long walk, hoping to find other friends. The duckling walks until he sees a large barn and different animals. There are chickens, a goat, and a cow. The duckling sees all the different animals and thinks, "Maybe the animals will be my friends."
He walks up to the other animals, feeling nervous. He hopes they will be kind, but when the animals see him, their faces change.
The cow loudly says, "Look at your neck! You are a very strange duck!"
The animals keep being mean, and the duckling frowns. He walks off to the other side of the farm, away from the animals.
scene11.prompt: What should he try and think after this?

choices.text: Never try to make friends again, since it is clear no one will want to be friends with him.
He should try and dye his feathers to match the ducklings so that the animals will want to be his friend.
Continue looking for kind friends.

text: Trying again when things go wrong is a good idea.

text: Everyone is different, and that is a good thing. The duckling should not change himself to make other animals happy.

text: The duckling decides to continue looking for kind friends.
He keeps looking for friends until it is winter.
The weather is colder, and the duckling's journey looking for kind friends is harder. It is hard to find other animals because many are hiding inside from the cold weather.
The duckling cannot stay warm and safe without friends and somewhere to sleep.
Later he spots a small house. He can see the smoke from the chimney. He knows smoke comes from fire, and knows that inside the cottage will be warm.

choices.text: Knock politely and ask if anyone is home.
Rush to the door and peck at it loudly to get attention.
Try climbing up and going in through the chimney.

text: The duckling decides to knock politely and ask if anyone is home.
Making a lot of noise might scare anyone inside the house. It is a good idea to be calm and make a plan.

text: The duckling goes up to the porch and knocks. A farmer comes out and sees the duckling. "Oh no! You must be freezing." She grabs a blanket and a warm bowl of food for the duckling.

The duckling feels better with the blanket and food. The farmer says, "There is a pond in a cave where the water will not freeze. There are other birds there who you can meet. I will take you there once you have had some rest!"
The duckling sleeps, and the next day he follows the farmer down to the cave. Inside, the duckling sees beautiful swans landing in the pond.

choices.text: Avoid the swans because he's afraid they will be mean to him.
Jump straight into the pond and make a splash to show he is funny!
Calmly say hi and ask to join them.

text: He will not know if they are mean if he does not talk to them. A good choice is to greet them calmly.

text: The duckling decides to calmly say hi and ask to join the swans.
He kindly waves his feathers. "Hi there... I have never seen birds like you. Is it alright if I join you in the pond?"
The swans look at him and smile. "Of course! You look just like we did when we were little!" one said.

The duckling is shocked to learn that he is not a duck at all. The swans tell him he is also a little swan. He learns now that by being true to himself and looking out for kind animals, he will find a place he belongs to be happy in.
